measurement.method: Straight: battery OFF, wheel moved by hand at the left front wheel, ruler held against the body, three settled alignments recorded receive-only (tx 0) and segmented from the journal with the approach direction derived from the recorded travel. Angle points: electrical team protractor measurement against a drawn reference line, battery OFF, USB power. Sign: type150 D50 firmware, battery ON, drive PWM 0, two-stick window; DIR latch and pin level agreed on every move.
measurement.connection_wiring_stop_means_checked_kst: 2026-09-18 08:05 user report: vehicle battery OFF, no wiring change beyond the electrical team moving steering DIR from D6 to D50, Mega + controller on the USB hub, vehicle stop switch present (confirmed 9/17-9/18, not re-asked)
measurement.notes: Straight adc 427 is the median of three body-referenced alignments recorded 08:19-08:23 (403 approached from the right, 427 and 442 approached from the left; within-window stability 1-2 adc, spread 39 adc ~= 2.2 deg). No systematic approach-direction effect appeared this session (the from-right value was the LOWEST, opposite to the ordering seen on 9/18 03:41 and 06:2x), so the spread is alignment repeatability, not hysteresis. Independent corroboration: 426.5 is the adc at which the electrical team's own MR(-17.9 deg, 108) and ML(+15.6 deg, 704) give the same gain on both sides (17.79 adc/deg); their own hand-aligned straights 318/354/370 give strongly asymmetric gains (11.7-14.6 vs 21.4-24.7). Corroboration only: equal gain either side of zero is not guaranteed for a single (left front) wheel under Ackermann geometry. UNRESOLVED: a ~75 adc (~4 deg) offset between this body-referenced straight and the electrical team's floor-line straights; only a straight-driving test can settle which is the vehicle's true 0 deg. Treat the zero as +-20 adc (~1.1 deg) repeatable and possibly biased by a few degrees until then. FOURTH alignment: the user re-aligned the wheel to straight by hand at about 08:41 and the board then read a rock-steady adc 432 over 99 receive-only frames (data/type150_identify_20260918_084402_prelive). The four body-referenced alignments are 403/427/432/442, mean 426, median 429.5; the adopted 427 lies within 3 adc of both, so it was not changed. This fourth value was captured as a start-position check and was not part of the segmented recording. FIRST CLOSED-LOOP RUNS 08:44-08:45 (battery ON, drive PWM 0) settled within 1-16 adc of four commanded targets with no overshoot beyond 2 adc and no hunting, so these bands are conservative: they can be tightened with recorded evidence later. 2026-09-18 14:25 CORRECTION: the '426.5 symmetric gain' corroboration assumes the electrical team's ANGLE ZERO is correct, which is exactly what is now in doubt, so its weight is reduced. A constant angle offset does not change the gain, so the team's 17.79 adc/deg stays usable; only the zero moves. The straight point is a candidate until an actual wheel angle is measured against the rear wheels.

points.note: electrical team protractor point L (median 906, n=31), reported as the rack's maximum travel. This session the motor at PWM 60 also stopped at 905-906, but a hand push reached 947-953, so the left end is compliant under force and is NOT a rigid index.

usable_limits.basis: Deliberately conservative outward stops for the first closed-loop trial, well inside the measured table (108..906): 280 ~= -8.3 deg and 620 ~= +10.9 deg by this table. They are a backstop against a sign or sensor fault, not the primary safety measure; the finite hold window, drive PWM 0, the operator and the vehicle stop switch are. Widen only with recorded evidence.

control.basis: Initial trial settings from this session's measurements, chosen to be stable rather than accurate. Steering travels ~357 adc/s at PWM 60 (446 adc in 1.25 s, data/dir_check_20260918_081108), i.e. ~18 adc per 50 ms status frame, and coasts 8-12 adc after the output is released (three observed releases). stop_band 25 therefore cannot be met more tightly than about one frame of travel, and restart_band 60 exceeds stop_band plus the observed coast so the loop holds instead of hunting. sensor_margin 30 admits a start position just outside the usable band. command_stale 400 ms tolerates a few missed host loops, sensor_stale 300 ms about six missed 50 ms status frames, reversal_neutral 250 ms of zero output before a sign flip on top of the type150 gate's own observed-zero rule. limit_policy 'reject' so an out-of-table target stops and locks instead of being silently clamped. Expect steady-state error up to about 37 adc (~2 deg) with these bands; tighten only after observing real runs.
